main_issue: Where to hold the farewell lunch after D can't eat at the Korean barbecue; whether to switch to a Japanese place (A, C, D) or consult the leaving colleague (B).

A-B.evidence: B questions changing the venue (8, 10, 13) and asks to ask her (26); A rejects: 'She said no... move on' (12, 14), 'let's not bother her with it. It's decided' (29).

A-C.evidence: C accepts the original plan with time worry (3), later 'Japanese is quick... just pick a place' (23, 27); A: 'He's right, we need to decide... I'll book it' (25, 29).

A-D.evidence: A first forgot, then accepts D's constraint (5, 7); D suggests Japanese (20), A agrees (21) and books it (29).

B-C.evidence: B wants to ask her what she'd like (26); C replies 'That will just take more time. Can we please just make a decision?' (27).

B-D.evidence: B asks D if it could work (10); D says it can't, but later 'Agent B has a point' (20) and offers Japanese; B still doubts Japanese (22).

C-D.evidence: D proposes Japanese as quick with options for everyone (20); C echoes 'Japanese is quick and has options for everyone' (23, 27).
